message: CREATE INDEX on appointments is not CONCURRENTLY, so writes to appointments wait until the index is built.
fix: Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, in a migration that does not run inside a transaction block.

message: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on appointments is written inside a transaction block (BEGIN at line 2). The manual says it cannot run in one, so the statement fails.
fix: Move the statement out of the BEGIN ... COMMIT block, into a migration of its own that your tool does not wrap in a transaction.

message: ADD COLUMN phone is NOT NULL and has no DEFAULT. The manual says a column without a default is filled with NULL and that a NOT NULL column cannot hold null values, so the statement fails when patients already has rows (this conclusion is the tool's own).
fix: Add the column with a constant DEFAULT, or without NOT NULL, fill the existing rows in batches, and add NOT NULL in a later migration.

message: The DEFAULT of ADD COLUMN created_at calls clock_timestamp(), which the manual names as volatile. A volatile DEFAULT rewrites the entire table and its indexes.
fix: Add the column without a default (or with a constant one), fill the existing rows in batches, then set the default for new rows with ALTER COLUMN ... SET DEFAULT.

message: ALTER COLUMN date_of_birth TYPE can rewrite patients and its indexes. The manual says it will normally do so, except when the USING clause does not change the contents and the old type is binary coercible to the new one, which the tool cannot judge.
fix: Add a column of the new type, copy the values in batches, move the application to it and drop the old column in a later migration; or confirm that this change needs no rewrite.

statement: ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN SET NOT NULL
message: SET NOT NULL on email scans all of patients to check that no row holds NULL, while the ALTER TABLE lock is held.
fix: Add CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID, run VALIDATE CONSTRAINT on it, then SET NOT NULL: the manual says the scan is skipped when a valid CHECK constraint proves that no NULL can exist.

message: ADD FOREIGN KEY constraint without NOT VALID scans all of appointments to check the existing rows, and updates to the table are locked out until the statement is committed. A foreign key also takes a lock on the referenced table.
fix: Add the constraint with NOT VALID, then run ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a separate statement.

message: ADD CHECK constraint without NOT VALID scans all of appointments to check the existing rows, and updates to the table are locked out until the statement is committed.
fix: Add the constraint with NOT VALID, then run ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a separate statement.

message: RENAME COLUMN starts_at TO start_time on appointments. Running application code, and the version of it that is still deployed, uses the old name and fails.
fix: Expand and contract: add the new column, write to both, backfill, move the application to the new name, and drop the old column in a later migration; or rename only when no old version of the application is running.

message: DROP COLUMN notes on appointments deletes the data of the column, and running application code that still reads or writes it fails.
fix: Expand and contract: stop all reads and writes of the column in the application first, keep the column for one release, copy what you need elsewhere, and drop it in a later migration.

message: DROP TABLE removes legacy_waitlist with its indexes, rules, triggers and constraints, and all of its data. Running application code that still reads or writes it fails.
fix: Expand and contract: stop all reads and writes in the application first, keep the table for one release (or rename it out of the way), copy what you need elsewhere, and drop it in a later migration.

message: TRUNCATE removes all rows of reminders and takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on each table, which blocks all other concurrent operations on it.
fix: Make sure that the data is meant to go. On a table that is in use, delete the rows in batches with a WHERE clause instead.

message: DELETE FROM appointments has no WHERE clause, so it deletes every row of the table.
fix: Add a WHERE clause. If every row is meant to go, say so in a comment, and on a large table delete in batches.

message: UPDATE patients has no WHERE clause, so it changes every row of the table.
fix: Add a WHERE clause. If every row is meant to change, say so in a comment, and on a large table update in batches.

message: LOCK TABLE rooms takes the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, which conflicts with locks of all modes and blocks even a plain SELECT, until the transaction ends.
fix: Take the weakest lock mode that does the job, or remove the statement when the command that follows takes the lock it needs by itself.

message: VACUUM FULL rewrites appointments into a new file and holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on each table while it does.
fix: Use a plain VACUUM, which does not take that lock, or run VACUUM FULL in a maintenance window when no application is using the table.

message: CLUSTER rewrites appointments and holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on it, so no other session can read or write the table until it is finished.
fix: Run CLUSTER in a maintenance window when no application is using the table.

message: VALIDATE CONSTRAINT appointments_patient_fk checks the existing rows of appointments. It takes only a SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock, so writes continue; it is the second step of the NOT VALID pattern.
fix: No change is needed. Run it in a migration of its own, so that the scan does not hold up other changes.

message: The body of a DO block is not read, so a statement inside it is not checked.
fix: Write the statements in the migration file itself, outside the DO block, so that they are checked.

message: The last statement of the file is not ended with a semicolon.
fix: End the statement with a semicolon, so that where it ends is not left to the tool that runs the file.
